Client summary
- Age/sex: 45, female
- Medical: Type 2 diabetes, on metformin, recent HbA1c 7.2%
- Goal: 12-week program focused on fat loss and improved glycaemic control
- Access: Full gym
- Important considerations: Avoid hypoglycaemia (though metformin alone rarely causes it), monitor blood glucose if symptomatic around exercise, prioritize progressive resistance training to improve insulin sensitivity, include aerobic and interval work, manage diet to create modest calorie deficit while stabilizing blood glucose (avoid severe restriction), ensure adequate protein and timing to reduce post-prandial spikes and maintain lean mass. Recommend she checks with her prescribing clinician if any med or dose changes are needed before program start; stop and seek medical advice for chest pain, sudden dizziness, severe hypoglycaemia symptoms.

Program overview (12 weeks)
Structure: 3 phases — Foundation (Weeks 1–4), Build/Intensity (Weeks 5–8), Peak/Recomposition (Weeks 9–12). Training frequency: 4 gym sessions/week: 3 resistance sessions (full-body emphasis, two higher-load strength sessions + one metabolic/conditioning/resistance-hybrid) and 1 dedicated aerobic/interval session. Optional active recovery (walking, mobility, yoga) 1–2 days/week. Progressive overload across phases. Mobility and warm-up before sessions; cool-down + brief stretching after.

Key targets
- Strength: improve compound strength (squat/hinge/push/pull) to preserve/raise lean mass.
- Cardio: build aerobic base and include 1 HIIT-type session to improve insulin sensitivity.
- Metabolic: 1 weekly higher-rep circuit to increase calorie burn and metabolic conditioning.
- Nutrition: modest calorie deficit ~300–500 kcal/day below estimated maintenance (aim 0.5–1% bodyweight loss per week initially), protein 1.4–1.6 g/kg bodyweight/day, carbohydrate distribution to support training and glycaemic control (lower glycaemic-load meals, focus on fibre and protein at main meals), timing: avoid long fast before exercise if risk of hypoglycaemia, consume small carb+protein snack before/after higher-intensity sessions as needed. Emphasize non-starchy vegetables, whole grains, legume/vegetable proteins, healthy fats. Regular meal spacing (3–4 hours) to blunt post-prandial spikes. Encourage weight loss target ~5–8% bodyweight over 12 weeks (individual).

Precautions & monitoring
- Metformin rarely causes hypoglycaemia by itself, but exercise increases glucose uptake. Teach client signs of low glucose (sweating, tremor, confusion, lightheadedness). Recommend checking capillary glucose before exercise if she feels uncertain or if blood glucose <5 mmol/L (90 mg/dL) or >15 mmol/L (270 mg/dL) — if low, consume quick carbs; if very high or ketotic, avoid high-intensity exercise and seek medical advice.
- Bring fast-acting carbs (juice, glucose tablets) to sessions initially.
- Hydration, footwear, and foot care (inspect feet daily).
- If any new symptoms (chest pain, syncope, unexplained breathlessness) stop exercise and seek medical attention.

Warm-up/cool-down (for each session)
- 6–8 minutes cardio at low–moderate intensity (rowing, bike, brisk walk)
- Dynamic mobility: hip hinges, leg swings, arm circles, thoracic rotations
- 2–3 warm-up sets for heavy lifts (if applicable) ramping reps
- Cool-down: 5–8 minutes easy cardio or walking and 5 minutes static stretching for major muscle groups

Phase 1: Foundation — Weeks 1–4
Goals: Build movement quality, baseline strength, aerobic base, begin calorie deficit and glycaemic-stabilizing nutrition.

Weekly structure (example)
- Day 1: Strength A (heavy-ish lower focus)
- Day 2: Cardio / Intervals (steady-state + short intervals)
- Day 3: Rest or active recovery (walk 30–45 min)
- Day 4: Strength B (heavy-ish upper focus)
- Day 5: Metabolic circuit (full-body, higher rep)
- Day 6: Optional light activity / mobility
- Day 7: Rest

Session details

Week 1–2
Strength A (45–60 min)
- Back squat (or goblet squat if mobility limited): 3 sets × 8–10 reps, RPE 6–7
- Romanian deadlift (dumbbell or bar): 3 × 8–10
- Split lunge (stationary): 2 × 10–12 each leg
- Leg press (machine): 2 × 12–15
- Plank: 3 × 20–30 s
- Farmer carry: 2 × 30–40 m

Strength B (45–60 min)
- Incline dumbbell press: 3 × 8–10
- Seated row (cable or machine): 3 × 8–10
- Overhead press (dumbbell): 2 × 10–12
- Lat pulldown: 2 × 10–12
- Glute bridge (weighted if possible): 3 × 12–15
- Pallof press (anti-rotation): 2 × 10 each side

Cardio / Intervals (30–35 min)
- 10 min steady aerobic warm-up (treadmill or bike easy)
- 12 × 1 min moderate intervals at RPE 6–7 with 1 min easy recovery (total ~24 min)
- Cool-down

Metabolic circuit (30–40 min)
- 3 rounds, 40 s work / 20 s rest between exercises, 60–90 s between rounds:
  - Kettlebell swing
  - Push-up (knees if needed)
  - Step-ups (alternating)
  - TRX rows
  - Bodyweight squat
- Aim controlled tempo; moderate intensity.

Weeks 3–4
- Increase load slightly on compound lifts (+5–10%), reduce reps to stated ranges; increase cardio intervals to 14 rounds or lengthen interval to 90 s work/90 s rest if tolerated.
- Add 1 extra set to one or two exercises per strength session.
- Maintain higher-protein nutrition and modest energy deficit.

Nutrition guidelines — Phase 1
- Energy: estimate maintenance caloric intake (trainer to calculate from client data). Aim for −300 to −500 kcal/day for steady fat loss. Avoid deficits >20% of maintenance initially.
- Protein: 1.4–1.6 g/kg bodyweight/day (spread across 3–4 meals). Example: if 70 kg, aim 98–112 g/day.
- Carbs: distribute around activity. Prioritize low–moderate GI carbs: rolled oats, basmati rice, sweet potato, legumes. Pre-workout small snack containing 15–30 g carb + 10–20 g protein if training >10–12 hours after meal.
- Fat: 25–35% of total calories, favor mono/polyunsaturated fats (olive oil, nuts, avocados).
- Fibre: target 25–35 g/day to blunt glycaemic spikes (vegetables, legumes).
- Meal spacing: eat every 3–4 hours (3 meals + 1 snack) to avoid large post-prandial excursions.
- Alcohol: limit, as it can affect glucose and calories.
- Hydration: 2–2.5 L/day unless contraindicated.

Glycaemic-specific advice
- Prioritize protein + fiber at breakfast to reduce morning glucose variability.
- If post-prandial glucose frequently >10–11 mmol/L (180–200 mg/dL), advise reducing meal carbohydrate portion or selecting lower GI options and increasing post-meal walking 10–20 minutes.
- Encourage consistent carb intake day-to-day — avoid large swings.

Phase 2: Build/Intensity — Weeks 5–8
Goals: Increase strength and volume, introduce heavier sets, incorporate structured HIIT and increased metabolic conditioning to accelerate fat loss and insulin sensitivity.

Weekly structure
- Day 1: Strength heavy lower (focus on 4–6 rep work)
- Day 2: HIIT (bike/sprints) + mobility
- Day 3: Strength heavy upper
- Day 4: Rest or active recovery
- Day 5: Full-body hypertrophy circuit
- Day 6: Optional long low-intensity steady-state (LISS) 40–60 min walk or bike
- Day 7: Rest

Session details

Weeks 5–6
Strength lower (60 min)
- Barbell back squat (or leg press if mobility): 4 sets × 5–6 reps (RPE 7–8)
- Romanian deadlift: 3 × 6–8
- Bulgarian split squat: 3 × 8 each leg
- Hamstring curl (machine): 3 × 10–12
- Core: deadbug 3 × 10 each side

Strength upper (60 min)
- Flat barbell or dumbbell bench press: 4 × 5–6
- Bent-over row or chest-supported row: 4 × 6–8
- Seated overhead press: 3 × 6–8
- Pull-ups or assisted pull-ups / lat pulldown: 3 × 8–10
- Face pulls: 3 × 12–15
- Farmer carry / loaded carry: 3 × 40–60 m

HIIT session (30 min)
- Warm-up 10 min
- 10 × 30 s all-out or RPE 8–9 on bike/row/sprints with 90 s easy recovery (or 1:3 work:rest)
- Cool-down 5–10 min

Full-body hypertrophy circuit (45–50 min)
- 3 rounds of:
  - Leg press 12–15
  - Dumbbell incline press 10–12
  - TRX row 12–15
  - Kettlebell swing 15
  - Walking lunges 12 each leg
  - Plank to side plank 30 s each
- Rest 90 s between rounds

Weeks 7–8
- Increase intensity: add sets (e.g., 5 × 5 on main lifts) or small load increases 2.5–5 kg when form maintained.
- HIIT: progress to 12 intervals or increase intensity (shorter rest).
- Consider one heavy single or double set on squat/bench near RPE 8 for neuromuscular stimulus if comfortable.

Nutrition guidelines — Phase 2
- Continue −300 to −500 kcal/day unless weight loss stalls; re-calculate maintenance if significant weight lost.
- Protein maintained at 1.4–1.8 g/kg (higher end during heavier phases).
- Carbs timed: larger portion around training sessions (pre and post). Post-workout meal with 20–30 g protein + 30–50 g carbs to support recovery and blunt post-workout hypoglycaemia.
- Continue fiber emphasis and whole-food carbs. Consider swapping some starchy carbs for more vegetables if caloric targets unmet.
- If glucose readings show post-exercise hypoglycaemia (rare on metformin but possible), add 10–20 g extra carb pre-session or reduce intensity; always carry fast carbs.

Phase 3: Peak/Recomposition — Weeks 9–12
Goals: Maintain strength, increase metabolic output, refine nutrition to maximize fat loss while protecting lean mass, focus on glycaemic control under slightly lower calories if needed.

Weekly structure
- Day 1: Strength (moderate heavy) + accessory
- Day 2: Interval + conditioning
- Day 3: Strength (compound emphasis)
- Day 4: Rest
- Day 5: Metabolic circuit (higher density)
- Day 6: LISS or mobility
- Day 7: Rest

Session details

Weeks 9–10
Strength sessions
- Compound focus: Squat 4 × 5, Deadlift variant 3 × 5, Bench 4 × 5, Row 4 × 6
- Accessory strength/hypertrophy: 3 sets × 8–12 for 3–4 exercises targeting weaknesses

Conditioning/intervals
- Mix of 20–25 min moderate intervals: 6 × 2 min hard / 1 min easy, or 12 × 60 s hard/60 s easy
- Add stairmill or sled pushes for metabolic variety

Metabolic circuit (higher density)
- 4 rounds AMRAP 12 min with 3–4 exercises alternating strength + conditioning, minimal rest

Weeks 11–12
- Deload approach in final week if needed: Week 12 reduce volume 20–30% to allow recovery and assessment.
- In Week 11 aim for last heavy efforts, maintain form and avoid chasing new 1RMs; focus on consistent load.

Nutrition guidelines — Phase 3
- If weight loss plateaued, consider small further deficit (additional −100–150 kcal/day) but do not drop protein. Avoid aggressive deficits to prevent loss of lean mass and impaired glycaemic control.
- Maintain protein 1.6–1.8 g/kg during final 4 weeks.
- Consider carbohydrate cycling: higher carbs (training days) 30–40% total calories, lower carbs (rest days) 20–25%, fat adjusted accordingly. This can help performance while reducing weekly calories.
- Continue meal timing strategies: protein at breakfast, carbs around workouts, fiber and healthy fats at other meals.
- Encourage post-meal walking 10–20 minutes after larger meals to blunt glucose peaks.

Sample daily meal plan (moderate 1,600–1,800 kcal example; adjust to client’s needs)
- Breakfast: Greek yogurt (150 g) + 30 g oats + 1 tbsp chia + handful berries + 1 tsp honey — approx 350 kcal (protein-focused, fiber)
- Mid-morning snack (pre-workout if morning): 1 small banana + 20 g whey or 1 boiled egg + 1 rice cake — 150–200 kcal
- Lunch: Grilled chicken salad (120–150 g chicken) with mixed greens, chickpeas 60 g, roast veg, 1 tbsp olive oil + lemon — 450 kcal
- Afternoon snack: Cottage cheese 100 g + cucumber or 10 almonds — 150 kcal
- Dinner: Baked salmon 120–150 g, steamed broccoli, 120 g sweet potato or 1/2 cup brown rice — 450 kcal
- Adjust portions to hit caloric target. Include 20–30 g protein at each main meal.

Practical coaching tips
- Track weight weekly and waist circumference every 2 weeks; avoid daily weigh-ins because of natural fluctuations.
- Keep a simple food log for 1–2 weeks each month to check adherence and carb distribution.
- Encourage consistent sleep (7–8 hours) and stress management — both affect blood glucose and weight loss.
- Re-assess HbA1c after ~3 months (post-program) with clinician; track fasting glucose and at-home post-prandial checks for short-term adjustments.
- If client experiences repeated pre/post-exercise glucose outside safe ranges, suggest contacting her diabetes clinician for medication review.

Progression & adjustments
- Increase load 2.5–5 kg when target reps are met with good form for two consecutive sessions.
- If recovery inadequate (persistent fatigue, sleep issues, loss of appetite), reduce volume by 10–20% and prioritize sleep, nutrition, and a deload week.
- If weight loss is faster than 1% bodyweight per week or symptoms of underfueling appear, increase calories slightly.

Outcome expectations
- With consistent adherence to program and nutrition, expect 4–10% bodyweight reduction over 12 weeks depending on starting weight and adherence. HbA1c improvements may lag but many people see reductions with weight loss and increased activity; expect modest reductions in fasting glucose and improved post-prandial control during the program, with A1c reassessment at ~12 weeks.

If you want, I can:
- Calculate specific calorie targets and macro breakdown if you provide current weight, height, and activity level.
- Provide printable week-by-week sheets per session for the client.
- Suggest specific progressions or alternative exercises for mobility or joint issues.
